The Jerusalem Icon of the Theotokos

Icons

Theotokos

The Jerusalem Icon of the Theotokos

Jerusalem Hodegetria · Ierusalimskaya

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

The Jerusalem icon has a received history extending from Gethsemane through Constantinople and Rus. The OCA explicitly calls its attribution to Luke a tradition.

[1] Opening paragraph

What is depicted

The displayed sixteenth-century Hodegetria shows Mary holding Christ, who raises a hand in blessing. Her other hand turns towards Him. The work is an identified historical Jerusalem-type icon; its surviving paint, frame and date belong to this particular object, not to a first-century portrait.

[2] Displayed work;file-level title,description,date and visual identification

History and tradition

The OCA recounts transfers to Constantinople in463, Korsun in988, then Novgorod and Moscow. It connects the icon with military deliverance and Prince Vladimir’s gift to the newly Christian Novgorod community. These are the commemoration’s received historical claims, not an independently reconstructed chain of custody for every surviving copy.

[1] Transfers and Novgorod

Published explanation

The account says the original was taken during the 1812 invasion and an authenticated copy replaced it in the Dormition cathedral. It commemorates the icon on October 12, November 13 and the fifth Saturday of Lent. Those printed dates and the movable observance remain distinct. The displayed sixteenth-century work is not presented as the lost original or as proof that Luke painted this surviving panel.

[1] 1812 and commemorations
